scenario: A hospital administrator will assign exactly seven medical interns—Fernandez, Gupta, Hollis, Ikeda, Jain, Kwon, and Liu—to exactly one of three departments: Cardiology, Emergency, or Pediatrics. Cardiology will receive exactly two interns, Emergency will receive exactly three interns, and Pediatrics will receive exactly two interns. The assignment must conform to the following conditions: Fernandez and Gupta are assigned to different departments. Hollis is assigned to Emergency. If Ikeda is assigned to Cardiology, then Jain is assigned to Pediatrics. Kwon and Liu are assigned to the same department. Gupta is not assigned to Pediatrics.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of interns to departments?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cardiology: Gupta, Ikeda; Emergency: Fernandez, Hollis, Kwon; Pediatrics: Jain, Liu

explanations.correct: All rules satisfied: Fernandez (Cardiology) and Gupta (Emergency) are in different departments; Hollis is in Emergency; Kwon and Liu are both in Pediatrics; Gupta is not in Pediatrics; and since Ikeda is in Cardiology, Jain is in Pediatrics as required.
explanations.B: Violates the rule that Fernandez and Gupta must be in different departments (both are in Cardiology).
explanations.C: Violates the rule that Kwon and Liu must be in the same department (Kwon in Cardiology, Liu in Pediatrics).
explanations.D: Violates the rule that Kwon and Liu must be in the same department (Kwon in Cardiology, Liu in Emergency).
explanations.E: Violates the rule that Kwon and Liu must be in the same department (Kwon in Emergency, Liu in Pediatrics).

questions.questionStem: If Ikeda is assigned to Cardiology, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: With Ikeda in Cardiology, the conditional forces Jain to Pediatrics. Cardiology needs one more intern, which must be Fernandez or Gupta (Kwon/Liu come as a pair and cannot both fit). If Gupta went to Cardiology, Fernandez would need to be elsewhere, but then Kwon/Liu must fill Pediatrics (2 slots) with Jain already there—overfilling Pediatrics. So Gupta cannot be in Cardiology, and since Gupta is barred from Pediatrics, Gupta must be in Emergency.
explanations.A: Fernandez could be in Cardiology or Pediatrics—not forced.
explanations.B: Correct — Gupta is forced into Emergency.
explanations.C: Jain must be in Pediatrics (forced by the conditional), not Cardiology.
explanations.D: Kwon/Liu together fill either Cardiology or Pediatrics; they are not in Emergency.
explanations.E: Liu could be in Cardiology (with Kwon) or Pediatrics (with Kwon)—not forced.

So the second Cardiology intern is Ikeda or Jain. If Ikeda is in Cardiology, Jain must be in Pediatrics. If Jain is in Cardiology, Ikeda is in Emergency. questions.questionStem: If Kwon is assigned to Cardiology, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: If Kwon is in Cardiology, Liu must also be in Cardiology (same-group rule). This fills Cardiology. So Fernandez, Gupta, Ikeda, and Jain split between Emergency (2 slots left, since Hollis takes one) and Pediatrics (2 slots). Gupta cannot be in Pediatrics, and Gupta cannot be in Cardiology (full), so Gupta must be in Emergency.
